items.text: Adults 21 and over may possess, buy and carry up to 1 ounce of marijuana, of which no more than 5 g concentrate. Smoking in a public place or open space is a petty offence; no use while driving or riding in an operating vehicle; property owners can ban use.

Kratom is legal to buy in Arizona under the Kratom Consumer Protection Act (A.R.S. 36-795 to 36-795.03), with limits on sellers: no sales to anyone under 18, no products with 7-hydroxymitragynine (a strong kratom alkaloid, called 7-OH) above 2% of the alkaloids, no synthetic alkaloids, and labels must state the mitragynine and 7-OH content. In December 2025 the Attorney General warned of synthetic 7-OH products being sold in the state and said she would seek a stronger law.

laws.rule: Drivers in Arizona may not hold or support a phone or other portable wireless device, or write, send or read texts, emails or internet data, while driving (A.R.S. 28-914). Voice calls through an earpiece, headphones or a wrist device, voice-commanded messages and hands-free navigation are allowed. The rule doesn't apply while parked or lawfully stopped.
laws.penalty_signal: Civil penalty of US$75 to US$149 for a first violation and US$400 for later ones, plus US$150 more if it causes a crash with a motorcycle (about A$107 to A$212, and A$568, at A$1 = US$0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026)

laws.rule: A driver who goes onto a flooded road that is barricaded because of flooding, and whose vehicle then stops working, is liable for the cost of the emergency response to remove them, their passengers or the vehicle (A.R.S. 28-910).
laws.penalty_signal: Liability of up to US$2,000 per incident (about A$2,840), on top of any other penalty

sites.name: Hopi villages
sites.what: Hopi communities on Hopi land; visitors are guests on private land and each village sets its own rules (Hopi Tribe).

access.photography: No recording of any kind in and around villages: photos, video, audio, sketching or note-taking
access.closures: Not all ceremonies are open; check posted signs or village community offices
access.guide: Tours with a Hopi-certified guide recommended (Hopi Arts Trail)

lore.text: Popular theories claim the Hopi 'ant people' were visitors from the sky; these are outside claims, not Hopi teaching.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: On Navajo Nation land: alcohol and illegal drugs are prohibited (Navajo law). Ask permission before photographing Navajo people; commercial photography needs a permit. Don't wander into residential areas. Firearms are banned on tribal lands (Navajo Tribal Code Title 17 s 1451).
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: All Navajo Nation areas are closed to non-Navajos without a valid camping, hiking or backcountry permit; entering without one is trespass. No climbing on monuments, sacred sites or buttes, no writing on rock walls, and no scattering of cremated remains. Don't disturb or remove plants, rocks or artefacts.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Navajo Nation Parks and Recreation Department.
culture-and-protocol.note: Navajo Nation lands only (Monument Valley, Canyon de Chelly, Antelope Canyon and others). Hopi and other nations have their own rules, not read here.

layers.authority: US National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park
layers.process: A backcountry permit is required for overnight camping outside Mather, Desert View and North Rim campgrounds, all Tuweep sites, and the North Rim from 16 Oct to 14 May. Day hikes need none. Apply on recreation.gov (permit 4675337). An early-access lottery runs for two weeks, opening on the 16th and closing at 5 pm MST on the 1st, four months before the start month; on the 1st of the following month remaining space opens to everyone. Fees: US$10 (about A$14) per application, non-refundable; US$15 per person per night below the rim and US$4 above it (about A$21 and A$6). Limits: two nights per designated site or campground per hike (corridor sites up to four nights from 15 Nov to 28 Feb), seven nights per use area, groups to 11. A few one-night corridor permits are sold in person at the Backcountry Information Center from 1 Mar to 30 Nov, no more than one day ahead; the page says availability is not guaranteed because of effects of an August 2026 flash flood. The Havasupai Tribe may charge an extra fee for South Bass and Pasture Wash trail visitors. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.

layers.authority: US Bureau of Land Management, Arizona Strip District (Coyote Buttes North, The Wave; reached from the Wire Pass trailhead in Utah)
layers.process: A permit is required for day hiking Coyote Buttes North (The Wave); there is no overnight camping. It comes from one of two lotteries on recreation.gov. Advanced Lottery: apply for a date four months ahead during the whole of one month (for example 1 to 31 January for May dates), choose up to three dates, results by email on the 1st of the next month, pay within 14 days; the application fee is US$6 (about A$8.50) and the BLM page says up to 48 people or 12 groups a day are awarded this way. Daily Lottery: for permits in the next few days, entered on recreation.gov through a mobile device inside a geofence (a location boundary) near the area; the in-person walk-in lottery ended in March 2022. Up to 64 people or 16 groups a day in total. Permit fee US$7 per person per day, and US$7 per dog (dogs must be on the permit); groups of six at most; everyone including infants is on the permit. Permits are non-refundable and non-transferable, cannot be rescheduled, and the site accepts credit card only. Campfires and launching or landing drones are prohibited in the wilderness. BLM says it cannot return calls from international numbers. Self-pay permits at Wire Pass do not cover Coyote Buttes North. The FAQ pages are dated 2022 in their publication field; fees and numbers should be confirmed on recreation.gov before use. Fees in US dollars; A$1 = USD 0.7040 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so US$1 is about A$1.42.
